synoptic.summary: High pressure with dry, stable air and valley inversions through Thursday; winds at the surface and aloft are light, so the local diurnal cycle decides which face works. Wednesday follows the normal pattern (drainage from 120°–150° in the morning, flow from 320°–360° from about 11:00). Thursday a light flow from 150°–180° aloft (up to 16–18 kt around 3,700–5,500 ft above the POM landings in the morning) keeps the launches on flow from 140°–200° all day and the usual afternoon switch is not forecast. Friday flow from 160°–200° strengthens ahead of an elongated trough (17–21 kt about 9,000 ft above landing), mixing deepens to over 4,000 ft and gusts reach 15–18 kt at launch; the trough brings rain and mountain snow on Saturday. No thunderstorm risk in the slots (thunder 0–1%).
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Southwesterly flow will start to increase ahead of an elongated trough on Friday. Current guidance has elevated winds increasing at the surface for western portions of the CWA. If they are able to break through the surface inversion then hazy conditions in the valleys could see improvement as early as Friday.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport (KSLC) sea-level pressure 1026.4 mb at 17:54 Tuesday, up 5 mb in 24 h (1021.4 mb) and up 1 mb in the last 3 h. Strong high = stable air, inversions and light gradient through Thursday; a fall is expected as the trough approaches Friday–Saturday (not yet in the data).

observations.summary: Readings from 17:15–17:39 Tuesday evening are current (under 45 min old at report time) but describe Tuesday's sunset, about 13.5 hours before the first slot. The valley is in its evening transition: Lehi 200° at 3 kt (gust 5) and South Valley Regional 210° at 2 kt have just turned to the up-valley drainage direction, while Salt Lake airport (270° at 5 kt), Provo (290° at 5 kt), Alpine (340° at 5 kt, gust 8) and Spanish Fork (359° at 5 kt, gust 6) still show the afternoon flow. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations.
